title: Decompose batcher heartbeat and KV-cache ownership to reduce contention and improve tail latency
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Context: The continuous batching subsystem currently mixes slot/lease heartbeats, ownership metadata for KV cache entries, and scheduler decision logic under a few coarse locks. This coupling has led to periodic p99 latency spikes during GC and lease churn, complicated failure modes during rolling upgrades, and brittle ad-hoc handoffs when shards rebalance.

Goal: Separate concerns by introducing a lean "lease heartbeat" service (epoch keeper) and a distinct KV-ownership coordinator so that slot scheduling and KV cache metadata updates are not serialized on the same hot paths. The change should reduce contention, improve tail latency under bursty ingress, and make future scheduler features (preemption, priority lanes) easier to implement.

This ticket covers design, prototype, metrics, a compatibility shim, and a staged rollout for the runtime cluster. It is explicitly a refactor/cleanup (no model behavior changes).
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end unit and integration tests cover lease transfer handshake, lost-heartbeat recovery, and concurrent KV ownership updates
Production canary shows p99 tokenization+serve latency reduced by at least 20% for the continuous-batcher workload under synthetic burst tests (same load profile used in perf-lab)
No increase in 5xx error rate during canary and 2% rollback window; all changes backward-compatible with current shard layout
New telemetry exported (lease_latency_ms, lease_conflicts, kvcache_owner_changes, heartbeat_dropped_count) and dashboard panels created in Grafana
Rollout documented with upgrade/rollback steps and a runbook for diagnosing ownership inconsistencies
technical_notes:
- Current coupling points: BatchCoordinator::heartbeat loop, KVCache::markOwner(), and SlotAllocator::assign(). Locks: global_lease_mutex and shard_owner_mutex.
- Proposed split: EpochKeeper (lease heartbeats, light-weight liveness), OwnershipCoordinator (durable owner mapping with compare-and-swap semantics), and SlotScheduler (fetches owner hints asynchronously).
- Use optimistic update protocol for owner claims (CAS on owner version + short-lived token). Store owner tokens in the compact kvcache metadata with a 64-bit epoch and monotonic counter to avoid full map locks.
- Compatibility shim: expose legacy markOwner API that enqueues changes to OwnershipCoordinator; drain mode supports both paths during migration.
- Observability: add span annotations to the heartbeat path and histograms for CAS contention.
- Backwards-compat: default behavior preserves current lease timeout values and heartbeat frequency; new epoch/owner fields are additive.
implementation_plan: Design doc in Confluence: runtime/epochkeeper-ownership-design (link provided in artifacts)
Prototype EpochKeeper as a standalone component in the runtime process with local in-memory state and telemetry (feature branch)
Introduce OwnershipCoordinator with CAS-based API and a migration-compatible markOwner queue
Integrate SlotScheduler to consult OwnershipCoordinator asynchronously and remove blocking calls from heartbeat loop
Add extensive unit tests and a perf microbenchmark (perf-lab harness) to quantify contention
Deploy canary to a small shard (canary-2) with increased telemetry retention, monitor for 48h
Full cluster rollout with staged percentage increases and a final cooldown before GA
risks: Race conditions during lease handoff leading to temporary double-ownership — mitigated by CAS + verification step
Telemetry blind spots during migration — mitigated by forcing detailed metrics in canary
Rollback complexity if ownership mappings diverge — mitigated via deterministic reconciliation job and runbook
Slight increase in memory footprint for ownership metadata per slot (expected <8 bytes per slot)
